podcasts.name: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Death and Legacy
podcast.body: Bruce Fairbairn passed away on May 17, 1999, at his home in Vancouver at the age of 49. Before his death, he established Little Mountain Sound in Vancouver, building it into one of North America's greatest recording studios. "On May 17, 1999, he was found dead at his home in Vancouver. It was just 49. But before he passed away, Bruce built his Vancouver recording studio, which is called Little Mountain Sound by the way, into one of the greatest recording studios in North America."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Early Career and Transition to Producer
podcast.body: Bruce Fairbairn started as a trumpet player in the Canadian 1970s band Prism. He began producing Prism's records in 1978 because the band could not afford an external producer, quickly gaining a reputation for his production skills. "He began as a trumpet player and a Canadian band from the 70s called Prism because the group couldn't afford a real producer, Bruce began producing Prism's records in 1978."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Extensive Production Success
podcast.body: Throughout the 1980s and 1990s, Fairbairn produced mega-platinum albums for numerous major rock bands, including Aerosmith, AC/DC, Bon Jovi, INXS, Kiss, Loverboy, Poison, The Scorpions, and Van Halen, accumulating close to 100 million album sales. "Throughout the 80s and 90s, he produced mega platinum albums for Erasmith and ACDC and Bon Jovi and Inaccess and Kiss and Leverboy and Poison, The Scorpions and Van Halen and a ton of others."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Mentor to Bob Rock
podcast.body: Bruce Fairbairn mentored Bob Rock, who started as an assistant producer at Fairbairn's Little Mountain Sound studio and later became his protégé. "Eventually, Bob started taking on his own clients and now his resume reads like some kind of who's who. ... And he got to where he is today thanks to the guidance and mentoring he received from another Canadian Superproducer, the late Bruce Fairburn."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Early Career and Mentorship
xref.body: Rock was a top employee and assistant producer at Bruce Fairbairn's Little Mountain Sound studio, where he developed into Fairbairn's protégé. He initially performed longer than Fairbairn, working with Paul Hyde into the late 1980s. "But he also had an assistant producer job at Little Mountain Sound with Bruce and he became so good at his job that he became sort of Bruce's protégé."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Early Production by Bruce Fairbairn
xref.body: In 1978, Bruce Fairbairn, a trumpet player in the band, began producing Prism's records because the group could not afford to hire an external producer. "He began as a trumpet player and a Canadian band from the 70s called Prism because the group couldn't afford a real producer, Bruce began producing Prism's records in 1978."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: From Assistant to Producer
xref.body: Malcolm Burn was an assistant at Grand Avenue Studios and was later hired by Daniel Lanois to run Kingsway Studios in New Orleans. Like Bruce Fairbairn and Bob Rock, he transitioned from a band member (Boys Brigade) into full-time production. "And one of the guys he hired to run the place was an assistant at Grand Avenue named Malcolm Bern. Malcolm used to be in a band-2 they were called Boys Brigade but like Bruce Fairburn and Bob Rock Malcolm eventually got into producing full-time."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Independent Production Success
xref.body: After becoming Bruce Fairbairn's protégé, Bob Rock began taking on his own clients, and his production resume grew to include a wide array of notable artists. "Eventually, Bob started taking on his own clients and now his resume reads like some kind of who's who."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Vancouver Music Scene Origins
xref.body: Bob Rock emerged from the Vancouver music scene, similar to Bruce Fairbairn. "Bob also came out of the Vancouver music scene."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
